sections.review:
This game was only playable due to Rangers' newly installed undersoil heating system.
Celtic looked rusty after a long lay off and McNeill surprisingly chose Nicholas and McCluskey at striker with the industrious McGarvey on the bench.
In a game of few chances Celtic edged the first half and McCluskey should have done better than hit the side netting with a fine opportunity.
Rangers scored in 72 minutes when Bett scored after Bonner had brought down Cooper with a clumsy challenge.
Celtic threw McGarvey on and they showed more urgency but could not grab an equaliser.

sections.trivia:
Paul McStay scores his first goal for Celtic in his first league game.   
  Celtic supporters association boycott the game in protest at Aberdeen reducing Celtic's ticket allocation but boycott fails as Celtic fans still pack the away end.
sections.review:
Celtic recovered well after going down to MacMaster's goal in the first minute.
The midfield four of Sullivan, McStay, MacLeod and Burns were excellent throughout and Provan's absence was not missed.
McCluskey hit a post and McGarvey missed a sitter from six yards before McCluskey equalised from the spot after Rougvie fouled McGarvey.
Celtic soaked up the pressure in the second half and MacLeod put them in front from a free kick when the ball deflected off the Aberdeen wall.
Miller was fortunate to stay on the park after a rugby tackle on McGarvey when he was clean through.
However McStay clinched it with a glorious third when he made space in the area and fired a left foot shot past Leighton.
McStay at only 17 was arguably the best player on the park and looks to have a wonderful future ahead.

sections.trivia:
Celtic make an enjoyable trip to Hong Kong.
Celtic were paid £20,000 for travelling to the Far East. Billy McNeill stated that Celts would have had handed back half of the fee had they lost.
sections.review:
Celtic sent a team out to the Far East to take part in this mini-tournament and play an exhibition game against Hong Kong Rangers. There was a free weekend as the team had previously been knocked out of the Scottish Cup on 13th February by Aberdeen.
Jimmy Bone, ex Celtic and St Mirren, and Steve Paterson, later of Inverness Cally Thistle and sacked Aberdeen manager, were playing for Hong Kong Rangers at that time.
Although 28,000 tickets were sold there was only an attendance of 5319 due to an atrocious period of heavy rain. The game was fortunate to take place and finish. Had it been a competitive match it may have been postponed.
The humidity was said to be stamina sapping.

sections.review:
Celtic went into this game with a depleted side. First choice strikers McGarvey, McCluskey and Nicholas were all out with injury and McGrain, Provan and Burns all played through the pain barrier despite being nowhere near 100% fit. In a make shift attack Tom McAdam was reinstated to the striker's role after a 3 year spell at centre half and young 19 year old forward Danny Crainie made his Old Firm debut.
It was a warm windy day and the pitch was fiery and bare in places. Celtic attacked from the kick off and Crainie sensationally scored after only 90 seconds. Burns ran from midfield and sent Sullivan clear on the right. His shot was sclaffed across goal and Crainie arrived at the back post to bundle the ball past Jim Stewart. After this goal Rangers came back at Celtic and Russell hit the bar after a fine free kick move with Cooper.
In 50 minutes McClelland gave away a foul with a needless foul on Crainie. From the free kick Burns crossed to McAdam who headed in at the back post. Rangers fought back with Derek Johnstone giving young Celtic centre half Davie Moyes a torrid time. Johnstone hit the bar and then Sullivan saved Celts when he headed a McClelland effort off the line.
Johnstone eventually scored with a fine volley which took a slight deflection off McGrain. He then gesticulated to the Celtic fans in the Jungle who had taunted him with needless offensive chants. Despite further Rangers pressure Celtic held on and McNeill hailed his walking wounded at the end.

The young Celtic players celebrated with the cup in front of the Celtic fans in the Broomloan stand at the end.

sections.trivia:
Celtic win consecutive league titles for the first time since 1974.   
  With Aberdeen having to win by 5 goals against Rangers they go 4-0 at half time as Rangers capitulate. It finishes 4-0.   
  Tommy Burns earns respect of fans by handing his jersey and boots over to disabled fans at the end of the game.   
  Celtic fans earn the wrath of Billy McNeill after a good natured pitch invasion after the final whistle.   
  Celtic players hoist Danny McGrain high after the League trophy is presented to him by Jim Farry.
sections.review:
Celtic are crowned the league champions.
At half time with the score 0-0 the Celtic fans learned that Aberdeen were leading Rangers 4-0 at half time. One more Aberdeen goal in the second half (and a winner for St Mirren) would nick them the title.
Celtic heard their nerve in the second half. Tommy Burns brilliantly created two goals for George McCluskey and Tom McAdam's header was adjudged to have gone over the line.
At the final whistle the fans celebrated joyously and the players danced all over the pitch before a good natured crowd invasion.
Injured Celts McGarvey, Nicholas, Conroy, and Sullivan could all be seen celebrating at the end.
Everyone remembers the 1986 League win against St Mirren but this one was just as good.
I don't know how to add the Celtic Underground Video Highlights, so if somebody else knows, feel free to add the widget. Thanks to CU for the video.
